To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ubiquitylation pathway can be used as an efficient tool for the chemical modification of artificial substrates and that the ubiquitylated products obtained can be further processed by proteases.
the ubiquitylated E1–S–thioester reacts readily with the thiol of a cysteine to produce a stable peptide bond.

the E1 enzyme can be used to produce ubiquityl thiolate, which can be transferred to a cysteine to yield a stable ubiquityl peptide bond, thus allowing the chemoenzzymatic ubiquitination of artificial substrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel tools for the chemical modification of Ub (Ulb) proteins, and the use of these tools to investigate the ubiquitin conjugation system.
the development of new methods for protein chemistry of ubiquitination.
the development of new tools for the chemical modification of Ub and UBLs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ubiquitin thioester is a reactive intermediate in the ubiquitylation reaction and that the thioester is formed by a nucleophilic attack of the thiol group of the ubiquitin-activa ting enzyme (E1) on the C terminus of ubiquitin, which is activated by ATP hydrolysis.
ubiquitin is an important protein for the cell and that it is involved in many cellular processes and that it is a protein with a high degree of conservation in eukaryotes.
ubiquityl (Ubl)-thioester is a versatile and powerful chemical handle that allows the chemoenzzymatic conjugation of Ub (Ulb) to artificial substrates, including proteins and other molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ubiquitin conjugation machinery is a powerful tool for the chemical modification of proteins and peptides.
the ubiquitylation reaction can be used to covalently attach Ub (Ubl)-like moieties to a protein or peptide of interest.
the E1-catalyzed ubiquityl thiolation of small molecules can be used to generate artificial substrates for DUBs and to probe the mechanism of E2 and E3 catalysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ubiquitylation of small peptides is possible and can be used to produce artificial Ub conjugates.

the ubiquitylation of small peptides can be achieved in vitro by the E1 enzyme, thus allowing the production of a large variety of Ub–peptide conjugates that can serve as probes to decipher the ubiquitylation pathways.
the Ub (Ubl)-S-E1 thiol ester is a versatile reagent for protein modification.
